reports.title: Realistic AI Avatars and Instagram/TikTok Automation: The Toolchain, Real Prices and the Official Rate Limits
reports.summary: The realistic-avatar stack is Higgsfield or Midjourney for the face, ElevenLabs for voice, HeyGen for lip-synced video, and Zernio for posting, about $110 a month at list prices. This report covers ranked sites and prices, disclosure and likeness rules, the official API caps (Instagram 50 posts/24h; TikTok ~15 posts/day per creator, private until audit), what happened to Instagress-style bots, and compliant alternatives. It contains no evasion methods.

reports.title: Selling Game Asset Packs in 2026: Where to Sell, What Sells, What Creators Really Earn and the AI Rules
reports.summary: Store cuts now favor sellers (Roblox 100% of net, itch 10% default, Fab 88%, CGTrader up to 85%, Unity 70%), but discovery is the hard part, and published small-seller earnings are modest. This report covers each store's AI disclosure rules, real best-sellers and prices, AI tools and copyright risk, pack ideas, costs and a 30-day plan.
reports.mascot_says: Sell a series, not a pile.

reports.title: Building an Obnoxious Genius: An Original AI Influencer for Higgsfield, 20 Viral Formats to Remake and a Full Character Bible
reports.summary: Uncanny signature-look AI characters (Jean Phil, Charles Robinson, Candy the greyhound) are winning by dropping one readable silhouette into every trend. This report lists 20 sourced viral formats to remake, plus a full bible for an original wild-haired know-it-all, Professor Smugworth: face, hair, outfits, palette, voice, Higgsfield prompts, 10 name checks, a first-10-posts plan and AI-label and likeness rules.
reports.mascot_says: Copy the format, never the face.

reports.title: Should Rich Buy a Kenworth Truck and Trailer? Costs, Pay and King County Work in the Pipeline
reports.summary: Used WA Kenworth T880s list at $42,500–$115,000 against $318,500 (pre-FET) new; used pups run $11K–$16K. King County public-works truck-and-trailer pay is $86.95/hr, and Seattle–Tacoma private rates are quoted at $130–$250/hr. New-venture insurance runs $14K–$20K+. Covers financing, WA permits, a labeled break-even illustration (~600 billed hours a year), the Sound Transit/WSDOT/King County pipeline and how a one-truck hauler gets on as a sub.
reports.mascot_says: Buy used, line up the work, then roll.

reports.title: A Coin Run by a Bot Team: Tokenomics, Holder Voting, the Cheapest Launch Path and Hot Crypto Markets
reports.summary: Launching costs only gas on pump.fun, Clanker or Zora; reported CEX entry runs from $20K–$75K (MEXC) to $500K–$2M+ (Binance). Proposes a 20% bot-compute treasury funded first by trading fees, quadratic Snapshot votes for features, seven original ideas, the hottest markets (record prediction-market volume, RWA, the AI-agent shakeout) and plain-language SEC/Washington risks.
reports.mascot_says: Let the bots do the work, let holders steer, and never promise a moon.

reports.title: Letting an AI Agent Post to X, Instagram and TikTok: Tools, Prices and a Setup for Every OMI Brand
reports.summary: Compares 15 options, from Zernio (formerly Late), Blotato, Postiz, Ayrshare and Buffer to Hootsuite, Sprout and the native APIs, on X/IG/TikTok support, MCP/API access, multi-brand support and stated prices. Top pick: Zernio's hosted MCP at $108/mo for 30 accounts plus X API usage, with Higgsfield for reviewed TikTok drops.
reports.mascot_says: Let the agent draft; let a human press Publish. And keep links out of X posts.

reports.title: An AI Course for Kids Under 14: Market, Competitors, Ideas, Needs and Costs
reports.summary: Kids already use AI widely (86% of 9–17s per Common Sense), but free school curricula own basic literacy and paid live AI classes cluster at grade 6+ with Python. The opening is a safety-first, parent-in-the-loop, project-based course for ages 10–13. Includes competitor pricing, the amended COPPA rule, California's new chatbot laws, needs, costs and a pilot plan.
reports.mascot_says: Teach them to build with AI and to doubt it. Keep their data out of it.

reports.title: AI Influencer Trends, Sep–Oct 2026: What CharacterGuard Ads Can Ride
reports.summary: Uncanny signature-look characters like Jean Philanthrope and Charles Robinson took off in weeks on Higgsfield-style motion transfer, and copycats followed within days. This report covers niches, hooks, tools, the fastest-growing accounts (sourced figures only), the stolen-face debate, 5 trends to ride and 3 CharacterGuard ad ideas.
reports.mascot_says: Go viral on Monday, get cloned by Friday. Lock it first.

reports.title: OMI Portfolio Review: Wash Wizardz, Get UI Now, DeepReach, FlirtFee and Fetch
reports.summary: Site-by-site fixes for the Open Mind Innovations companies, from unbacked trust claims and 8–11 MB pages to missing legal pages and a public investor form, plus bot-team plans for FlirtFee, DeepReach and Get UI Now.
reports.mascot_says: Strong offers up top, thin proof underneath. One basics pass helps every site.

reports.title: Pre-Flight for Vibe Coders: An App Store Rejection Scanner and 5 Sibling Ideas
reports.summary: Apple rejected 2.09M of 9.1M submissions in 2025, but pre-submission checkers are already crowded at $2.99–$199. The opening is a scanner built for vibe coders that checks the web wrapper, the backend and AI consent together. Five sibling ideas are ranked alongside it.

reports.title: 15 Low-Barrier Creative Aftermarket Opportunities for Optimus
reports.summary: Optimus is being built but not sold. These are 15 fun, low-capital aftermarket ideas (costumes, shells, decals, booths, wranglers), split into ones you can start now on robots you can rent today and ones that wait for robots in homes.
reports.mascot_says: Every robot deserves an ugly holiday sweater.

reports.title: 10 Micro-SaaS & Low-Maintenance Niche Opportunities
reports.summary: Ten single-purpose services built on the CharacterGuard pattern (free check, one-time kit, cheap watch), ranked on margin, maintenance, speed, and cited demand. SMS registration readiness and inbox-authentication fixes lead.
reports.mascot_says: Best niches had a hard rule behind them and a free check that can say ‘stop.’
